title: Quadratic Forms and Automorphic Forms
extended_summary:
This paper is a set of revised lecture notes on quadratic forms and automorphic forms, originally prepared for a graduate-level Arizona Winter School course. It surveys foundational theory rather than reporting an empirical study. The text develops basic definitions and classification results for quadratic forms over fields and rings, including equivalence, direct sums, orthogonal decomposition, local invariants, lattice duals, Jordan decomposition, and local-global principles such as the Hasse-Minkowski theorem.

A major second theme is the connection between quadratic forms and modular/automorphic forms through theta functions. The paper explains how theta series encode representation numbers of quadratic forms, why they converge, and how Poisson summation leads to modular transformation laws. It then situates these theta series inside the theory of modular forms, including weight, level, character, cusp forms, and Eisenstein series, and uses these ideas to discuss asymptotic representation results such as Tartakowski's theorem.

The intended audience is graduate students in mathematics, and the context is a theoretical lecture-note setting rather than a classroom intervention or education study. No educational population, teacher subgroup, school context, or generative-AI-related intervention is studied. The conclusions are mathematical: they summarize classical results and methods and provide a pathway from quadratic forms to automorphic forms and related arithmetic applications.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a mathematics lecture note / survey on quadratic forms and automorphic forms, not an empirical education or AI intervention study. It contains no K-12 design, participants, outcomes, or evaluation methodology relevant to the research topic.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational intervention or student/teacher outcome is evaluated, so there is no impact evidence to code for K-12 settings, teacher subgroup differences, or school context effects.
